input.strategy_title: Default Vector Store for Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag
input.strategy_markdown:
## Summary

RHOAI must provide a default vector store that is available out-of-the-box — without manual setup — so that Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag continue to function when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution image. Today these capabilities depend on an inline vector store provider bundled within the Llama Stack process; removing it (per RHAISTRAT-7474) will break them unless an alternative is available at the platform level.

## Problem Statement

Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag currently rely on an inline Milvus provider embedded in the Llama Stack distribution image to store and retrieve vector embeddings. This inline provider runs inside the Llama Stack process itself.

RHAISTRAT-7474 proposes removing inline providers from the Llama Stack distribution to improve GA readiness — shipping only what can be tested and maintained at scale, and aligning with Llama Stack's primary use case as a remote API server. However, no platform-level alternative exists today. If inline providers are removed without a replacement, any RHOAI user relying on Gen AI Studio's RAG capabilities or Auto Rag will lose functionality entirely — there is no workaround short of manually provisioning and configuring an external vector database.

Users expect vector storage to "just work" when they use Gen AI Studio or Auto Rag. The current out-of-the-box experience must be preserved even as the underlying architecture evolves.

## Affected Customers

* All RHOAI customers using Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities
* All RHOAI customers using Auto Rag
* This is a platform-level product dependency: these features cannot function without a vector store

## Business Justification

* **Product integrity:** Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag are GA-track capabilities in RHOAI. Removing the inline vector store without a replacement breaks shipped product functionality for every user of these features.
* **Blocking dependency:** RHAISTRAT-7474 (removing inline providers for GA readiness) cannot proceed until this RFE is resolved. Silas Brenmark (Gen AI Studio lead) has identified this as a blocker.
* **User experience:** RHOAI differentiates on integrated, opinionated defaults. Requiring users to manually provision and configure a vector database before they can use the playground or Auto Rag degrades the out-of-the-box experience that customers expect from the platform.

## Acceptance Criteria

* \[ \] A default vector store is available out-of-the-box on RHOAI without requiring users to manually provision or configure external infrastructure
* \[ \] Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] Auto Rag functions with the default vector store with no loss of current capability
* \[ \] The default vector store runs as a separate process, decoupled from the Llama Stack instance (not an inline provider)
* \[ \] The default vector store is scoped appropriately for multi-tenant environments (e.g., per-namespace isolation)
* \[ \] The default vector store is lightweight enough to run in resource-constrained environments without imposing significant overhead

## Success Criteria

* Users of Gen AI Studio and Auto Rag experience no functional regression when inline providers are removed from the Llama Stack distribution
* No additional manual setup steps are required for RAG workflows compared to the current experience
* RHAISTRAT-7474 is unblocked and can proceed to implementation

## Open Questions

* What is the preferred scoping model — per namespace, per Llama Stack instance, or both? (Silas noted per-namespace is preferred for isolation, but Auto Rag may need per-instance scoping)
* Should users have a migration path from the default vector store to a production-grade vector database? (Bram Sundqvist raised the importance of aligning with commonly-used vector DB providers for easier migration)

## Strategy (AI Generated by Agentic SDLC Pipeline)

> **Note:** The full strategy exceeds Jira's description size limit and is stored as an attachment: `RHAISTRAT-8004-strategy.md`.

## Staff Engineer Input

**Correction 1 — OGX does not auto-provision PostgreSQL.** OGX defaults to SQLite for storage (`storage.kv.type: sqlite`, `storage.sql.type: sqlite` in the OGXServer CRD). The odh-dashboard gen-ai BFF hardcodes SQLite when creating OGXServer instances for the playground (`kv_sqlite` and `sql_sqlite` in `llamastack_config.go`). PostgreSQL is a supported backend but must be user-configured with an explicit `connectionString` secret. The strategy's claim that "every LlamaStackDistribution instance requires a PostgreSQL database" is incorrect — introducing PostgreSQL is new work, not an extension of existing infrastructure.

**Correction 2 — A Red Hat PostgreSQL image with pgvector already exists.** The `registry.redhat.io/rhel9/postgresql-16` image includes pgvector out of the box — confirmed in the [sclorg/postgresql-container Dockerfile](https://github.com/sclorg/postgresql-container/blob/master/16/Dockerfile.rhel9) (`INSTALL_PKGS="$INSTALL_PKGS pgvector"`). PostgreSQL 18 (RHEL 9) also includes pgvector. Furthermore, the model-registry-operator already uses `postgresql-16` as its auto-provisioned database image, and `RELATED_IMAGE_POSTGRESQL_16_IMAGE` is already present in the rhods-operator CSV for disconnected installs. No custom image build is needed. No Konflux onboarding is needed. The 1-2 sprint image onboarding estimate in the strategy can be eliminated.

**Architectural direction — platform-level database vs. self-provisioned.** Multiple RHOAI components now need PostgreSQL (model-registry, MLflow, and now OGX for pgvector). The preferred long-term direction is a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL managed via the DSC, where each component consumes a connection string rather than self-provisioning. A shared platform-provided PostgreSQL via DSC will not be available until RHOAI 3.6. For 3.5, Gen AI Studio must provision its own PostgreSQL instance.

**Operator dependency for self-provisioning (RHAISTRAT-7164).** Self-provisioning PostgreSQL following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator for Gen AI Studio. The ogx-k8s-operator is upstream and cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. The dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164, In Progress) would provide this operator layer. This is a hard dependency — until RHAISTRAT-7164 delivers, there is no RHOAI-controlled operator where PostgreSQL lifecycle management can live. It will be challenging to commit this strategy to a specific release until that dependency is delivered.

**Fallback if RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time.** If the dashboard modularization is not ready for 3.5, the fallback is to require customers to bring their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Playground. Users would manually configure the OGXServer CR spec with their PostgreSQL connection details. This aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the Playground largely abstracts OGX from users. The development team should define a go/no-go gate for this decision as part of sprint planning.

**Decouple from Auto Rag.** Auto Rag integration with Gen AI Studio (RHAISTRAT-7824) is targeting RHOAI 3.6. This strategy should validate pgvector only for Gen AI Studio Playground RAG workflows. Auto Rag compatibility with pgvector will be addressed in RHAISTRAT-7824's scope. Remove Auto Rag from affected components, impacted teams, acceptance criteria, and validation requirements.

**Performance and index thresholds — dev experimentation scope.** The default pgvector instance is meant for development experimentation, not production usage. Strict latency SLAs (p50/p95/p99) are not required. The sprint 1 benchmark should capture the inline Milvus baseline and verify pgvector is in the same order of magnitude, not meet a specific threshold. Typical Playground RAG usage involves small document sets — flat scan (no index) is sufficient for the default. Users with production-scale vector workloads should use an external vector database. Remove open questions about latency thresholds, corpus size ranges, and index type selection.

**PostgreSQL resource sizing.** Reference the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL resource requests/limits as the starting point. Adjust based on sprint 1 benchmarking if needed.

**Alternative fallback — BFF-managed PostgreSQL provisioning.** If RHAISTRAT-7164 does not land in time, an alternative to requiring customers to bring their own PostgreSQL is to have the gen-ai BFF provision the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance directly, similar to how the BFF currently provisions guardrails infrastructure. The BFF would create the PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and Secret when a playground with RAG is configured, if one does not already exist in the namespace. Caveats: (1) the implementation must be designed for portability — when the platform-provided shared database becomes available (3.6), the BFF should consume the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning; (2) lifecycle management of the PostgreSQL instance must be carefully considered — the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention.

**Existing remote vector store implementation is reusable.** Per the engineering team, the existing remote vector store implementation can be largely reused for pgvector integration. The majority of the work effort is around infrastructure and provisioning of the PostgreSQL/pgvector database, not the vector_io provider integration itself.

**Correction 3 — Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations.** The OGX vector_io provider configuration (`remote::pgvector` via `ENABLE_PGVECTOR`) is completely separate from OGX's application storage backend configuration (`storage.kv.type`, `storage.sql.type`). This strategy only needs to configure the pgvector vector_io provider — it does not change the application storage backend, which remains on its existing default (SQLite). There is no SQLite-to-PostgreSQL migration concern because the application storage is not being touched. Remove any references to consolidating vector and application storage in a single database, and remove any SQLite-to-PostgreSQL upgrade path considerations.

# Operator-based self-provisioning of the default pgvector instance

> Conditional branch A — instantiated only if the provisioning go/no-go decision selects operator-based self-provisioning (the dashboard operator modularization, RHAISTRAT-7164, delivers a RHOAI-controlled operator layer in time for the target release).

## Description

This epic implements out-of-the-box provisioning of the default vector store using the RHOAI-controlled operator layer delivered by the dashboard operator modularization (RHAISTRAT-7164). Self-provisioning PostgreSQL for Gen AI Studio following the model-registry-operator pattern requires a RHOAI-controlled operator; the upstream ogx-k8s-operator cannot carry RHOAI-specific provisioning logic. When a Gen AI Studio playground with RAG is configured, the operator provisions a PostgreSQL instance with pgvector (using the existing Red Hat `postgresql-16` image, which includes pgvector out of the box) and wires the OGX instance to use it as its vector I/O provider.

The implementation must remain portable to the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL planned for RHOAI 3.6: the consuming configuration is a connection string, so the shared database can replace self-provisioning without redesign.

## Scope

- Implement PostgreSQL/pgvector lifecycle management in the RHOAI-controlled operator layer delivered by the dashboard operator modularization: provisioning the database Deployment, Service, persistent storage, and credentials Secret per namespace, following the model-registry-operator's auto-provisioning pattern as the reference implementation.
- Wire the provisioned instance into the OGX server configuration for playgrounds with RAG, activating the remote pgvector vector I/O provider with the provisioned connection details.
- Scope instances per namespace for multi-tenant isolation (per-namespace is the resolved scoping direction; the per-instance consumer, Auto Rag, is handled in RHAISTRAT-7824).
- Apply resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL sizing, adjusted per the benchmark recommendation where available.
- Design for portability: the OGX configuration consumes a connection string, so a platform-provided shared database (RHOAI 3.6) can replace self-provisioning without changes to the consuming side.
- Handle lifecycle end-to-end in the operator: creation, upgrade, credential management, and cleanup when the owning playground (or its namespace resources) is deleted.

Out of scope: the OGX-side provider enablement (delivered by the distribution's remote pgvector provider configuration); benchmarking; Auto Rag compatibility (RHAISTRAT-7824); the platform-shared database itself (RHOAI 3.6).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user who creates a Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities gets a working default vector store with no manual provisioning or external infrastructure configuration (out-of-the-box experience preserved).
- The PostgreSQL/pgvector instance (Deployment, Service, persistent storage, credentials Secret) is provisioned and managed by the operator, and is cleaned up when the owning playground is deleted.
- Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function end-to-end against the default vector store with no loss of current capability (document ingestion, retrieval, and query flows).
- Vector store instances are isolated per namespace; one namespace's playground cannot read another namespace's vector data through the default store.
- The provisioned instance's resource requests/limits follow the agreed sizing (model-registry-operator reference, adjusted per benchmark where applicable) and run without significant overhead in resource-constrained environments.
- The OGX-side wiring consumes a connection-string style configuration, so a platform-provided shared PostgreSQL can replace the self-provisioned instance without changes to the consuming configuration.
- The pgvector-capable PostgreSQL image reference used for provisioning is resolvable in disconnected installs (the related image env var already present in the rhods-operator CSV).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — default vector store available out-of-the-box without manual provisioning: delivered by operator-based self-provisioning.
- **HLR-2 (P0)** — playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability: end-to-end validation acceptance criteria above.
- **HLR-4 (P1, bundled)** — multi-tenant scoping (per-namespace isolation): a property of the same provisioning surface; bundled rather than split.

# BFF-managed provisioning of the default pgvector instance

> Conditional branch B — instantiated only if the provisioning go/no-go decision selects BFF-managed provisioning (the dashboard operator modularization does not land in time, and the team opts to preserve the out-of-the-box experience rather than requiring bring-your-own PostgreSQL).

## Description

This epic implements out-of-the-box provisioning of the default vector store directly in the Gen AI Studio backend-for-frontend (the gen-ai BFF), as the alternative to an operator-based approach when the RHOAI-controlled operator layer is not available in the target release. Following the pattern the BFF already uses for guardrails infrastructure, the BFF creates the PostgreSQL/pgvector instance — Deployment, Service, persistent storage (PVC), and credentials Secret — when a playground with RAG is configured and no suitable instance exists in the namespace, using the existing Red Hat `postgresql-16` image (pgvector included). The OGX instance is then wired to use it as its vector I/O provider.

The Staff Engineer Input flags the caveats that shape this epic: the BFF is not an operator with a reconciliation loop, so cleanup on playground deletion, handling of pod restarts, and credential rotation need explicit design attention; and the implementation must be designed for portability, so that when the platform-provided shared PostgreSQL becomes available (RHOAI 3.6) the BFF consumes the shared connection string rather than self-provisioning.

## Scope

- Implement provisioning logic in the gen-ai BFF: when a playground with RAG is configured and no PostgreSQL instance exists in the namespace, create the pgvector-capable PostgreSQL Deployment, Service, PVC, and credentials Secret; reuse the existing instance when one is already present.
- Wire the provisioned instance into the OGX server configuration for the playground, activating the remote pgvector vector I/O provider with the provisioned connection details.
- Implement lifecycle handling explicitly (no reconciliation loop): cleanup of the database resources when the owning playground is deleted; recovery from BFF pod restarts (idempotent re-check of existing resources); a defined approach to credential rotation.
- Scope instances per namespace for multi-tenant isolation (per-namespace is the resolved scoping direction; the per-instance consumer, Auto Rag, is handled in RHAISTRAT-7824).
- Apply resource requests/limits starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL sizing, adjusted per the benchmark recommendation where available.
- Design for portability: prefer consuming an existing connection string when one is provided (the RHOAI 3.6 platform-shared database path) over always self-provisioning.

Out of scope: the OGX-side provider enablement (delivered by the distribution's remote pgvector provider configuration); benchmarking; Auto Rag compatibility (RHAISTRAT-7824); operator-based provisioning.

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user who creates a Gen AI Studio playground with RAG capabilities gets a working default vector store with no manual provisioning or external infrastructure configuration (out-of-the-box experience preserved).
- The PostgreSQL/pgvector Deployment, Service, PVC, and credentials Secret are created by the BFF only when absent in the namespace, and an existing suitable instance is reused rather than duplicated.
- Gen AI Studio playground RAG workflows function end-to-end against the default vector store with no loss of current capability (document ingestion, retrieval, and query flows).
- Deleting a playground cleans up the database resources it caused to be provisioned (or documents and implements the deliberate retention policy decided in design).
- A BFF pod restart does not leave orphaned or broken database resources: re-running the provisioning path is idempotent.
- Credential rotation is handled per the designed approach without breaking existing playground RAG workflows.
- Vector store instances are isolated per namespace; one namespace's playground cannot read another namespace's vector data through the default store.
- The provisioned instance's resource requests/limits follow the agreed sizing (model-registry-operator reference, adjusted per benchmark where applicable) and run without significant overhead in resource-constrained environments.
- The BFF consumes a provided shared connection string in preference to self-provisioning when one is available, demonstrating the RHOAI 3.6 portability path.
- The pgvector-capable PostgreSQL image reference used for provisioning is resolvable in disconnected installs (the related image env var already present in the rhods-operator CSV).

## HLR Traceability

- **HLR-1 (P0)** — default vector store available out-of-the-box without manual provisioning: delivered by BFF-managed provisioning.
- **HLR-2 (P0)** — playground RAG workflows function with the default vector store with no loss of current capability: end-to-end validation acceptance criteria above.
- **HLR-4 (P1, bundled)** — multi-tenant scoping (per-namespace isolation): a property of the same provisioning surface; bundled rather than split.

# Bring-your-own PostgreSQL support for playground RAG

> Conditional branch C — instantiated only if the provisioning go/no-go decision selects bring-your-own PostgreSQL (neither operator-based nor BFF-managed provisioning is viable for the target release).

## Description

This epic implements the deliberate fallback in which customers provide their own PostgreSQL for RAG capabilities in the Gen AI Studio playground: users (or administrators) configure the OGXServer custom resource spec with their PostgreSQL connection details, and the playground's RAG workflows run against that database using the remote pgvector vector I/O provider. The Staff Engineer Input notes this aligns with the breaking changes introduced in OGX 1.0, even though the playground largely abstracts OGX from users — so this epic also carries the burden of making the configuration path as discoverable and low-friction as the playground permits. The end-to-end user-facing setup documentation for this configuration path is a primary work product and is delivered by a separate docs-authoring epic in this branch, scheduled docs-last after this implementation so it is technically reviewed against the configuration support as built.

## Scope

- Support and validate the configuration path by which a user-supplied PostgreSQL (with pgvector) is attached to an OGX instance for playground RAG: OGXServer custom resource spec fields and the credentials Secret carrying connection details.
- Surface the bring-your-own requirement in the Gen AI Studio playground where the abstraction would otherwise hide it: clear indication when no default vector store is available and RAG is requested, with guidance to the configuration path.
- Validate that the configuration path works end to end with the remote pgvector vector I/O provider enabled in the OGX distribution (document ingestion, retrieval, and query flows against a user-supplied database).
- Confirm per-namespace behavior: user-supplied instances and their credentials are referenced and scoped within the owning namespace.

Out of scope: the OGX-side provider enablement (delivered by the distribution's remote pgvector provider configuration); provisioning a default instance (this branch exists precisely when that is not viable); benchmarking; Auto Rag compatibility (RHAISTRAT-7824); the end-to-end user-facing setup documentation and its clean-environment walk-through (delivered by the docs-authoring epic of this branch).

## Acceptance Criteria

- A user-supplied PostgreSQL with pgvector, configured via the OGXServer spec and a credentials Secret, serves vector I/O for playground RAG workflows, verified end to end (document ingestion, retrieval, and query flows).
- The playground clearly indicates when RAG is unavailable because no vector store is configured, and points to the documented configuration path.
- Credentials are supplied via Secret references, never inline in the custom resource spec or exposed in process arguments.

## Description

- Vector storage and application storage are independent configurations. - Support wiring the provider's connection details (endpoint, credentials) via the distribution's existing secret-handling mechanisms (environment variables and `_FILE`-suffixed secret resolution).
- Document the configuration path for pointing the vector I/O provider at an external, production-grade vector database — the migration path from the default store for users whose workloads outgrow it.

# Benchmark pgvector against the inline Milvus baseline and set default resource sizing

- Compare results and record whether pgvector is within the same order of magnitude as the baseline (order-of-magnitude comparison, not a fixed threshold).
- Confirm (or refute) that flat scan (no vector index) is sufficient for typical playground document sets, and record the corpus-size boundary if one is observed.
- Produce the resource sizing recommendation (requests/limits) for the default pgvector instance, starting from the model-registry-operator's PostgreSQL sizing, adjusted based on the measured results.
